<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

The slash command handler hard-codes the `extra` CI tier (`tag_extra`, `_run_extra_ci`, a workflow display name). This has two problems:

- **It already misses a workflow.** `run-ci-extra` gates both `pr-test-extra.yml` and `pr-test-amd-extra.yml`, but `/run-extra-ci` only re-runs the first.
- **It does not scale.** Each new tier (`run-ci-mlu`, `run-ci-ppu`, ...) would need the same set of edits again.

## Modifications

- **Registry.** Add `scripts/ci/opt_in_ci_tiers.json` to map selections to workflow files and an optional opt-in label. The shared `extra` tier contains NVIDIA and AMD extra; `nv` selects NVIDIA base/shared checks without adding a hardware label.
- **Compatible defaults.** With no arguments, `/run-ci`, `/run-base-ci` and `/tag-and-rerun-ci` use the existing broad retry path, including eligible hardware. Existing label, permission and path gates still apply. Legacy commands retain their ignored-suffix behavior.
- **Explicit selections.** `/run-ci nv` reruns only existing NVIDIA base/shared checks at the current commit, including successful runs. Missing path-filtered workflows are skipped. This selection does not restrict hardware eligibility on future pushes.
- **Structured aliases.** `/run-ci <tier>` equals `/run-<tier>-ci`. `/run-extra-ci <hardware>` equals `/run-<hardware>-extra-ci` when that tier is registered; otherwise it retains the legacy ignored-suffix behavior. New `/run-ci` aliases reject unknown or multiple arguments.
- **Shared extra.** `/run-extra-ci` and `/run-ci extra` rerun both NVIDIA and AMD extra using `run-ci-extra`. Hardware-specific extra tiers are deferred to a follow-up. Legacy `/tag-and-rerun-ci <tier>` adds labels and retries broadly.
- **Gate and validation.** Use generic `require-label` for registered tiers in `pr-gate.yml`, while retaining the legacy `require-run-ci-extra` input and its independent label check for existing callers such as Xeon. The registry linter checks labeled tiers against their workflow gates and supports selections with `label: null`.
- **Docs.** Update the contribution guide, `.github/FOLDER_README.md` and the `ci-workflow-guide` skill.

Once a hardware workflow follows the opt-in gate and event conventions, adding its command requires only a registry entry. MLU and PPU are left to follow-ups because their workflows must first drop the `labeled` trigger. They are not currently registered.

## Validation

- 8,152 offline mocked compatibility, alias, permission and missing-run cases passed. No new repository test files were added.
- Applicable commit hooks and registry validation passed.
- The gate compatibility fix passed merged-tree input checks across 110 reusable-workflow calls and 480 event/input/label cases.
- Live hardware CI is not yet validated. Mintlify checks could not run because `mint` is unavailable locally.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

 |------|------|
 | `.github/workflows/pr-test.yml` | Main workflow — all stages, jobs, conditions, matrix definitions |

@@ -390,25 +391,43 @@ group: pr-test-{event_name}-{branch}-{pr_sha}-{stage}
 | Command | Effect |
 |---------|--------|
 | `/tag-run-ci-label` | Adds `run-ci` label to PR |
-| `/tag-run-ci-label extra` | Adds both `run-ci` and `run-ci-extra` labels |
+| `/tag-run-ci-label <tier> [<tier> ...]` | Also adds each tier's opt-in label (e.g. `run-ci-extra`); unrecognized suffixes are ignored |
 | `/rerun-failed-ci` | Reruns failed jobs in the latest workflow run |

-| `/tag-and-rerun-ci extra` | Adds both `run-ci` and `run-ci-extra` labels + reruns failed |

+| `/run-ci`, `/run-base-ci`, `/rerun-base-ci` | With no argument, aliases of `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, with the same broad retry scope and independent labeling/retry permissions. With one registered tier argument, equivalent to `/run-<tier>-ci`, including green runs and requiring both permissions. E.g. `/run-ci extra` equals `/run-extra-ci`. |
+| `/run-ci nv`, `/run-base-ci nv`, `/run-nv-ci` | Adds `run-ci` and reruns NVIDIA base/shared checks only, including green runs. No extra or other-hardware workflows. Existing hardware labels are kept; future pushes follow the existing workflow gates. |
 | `/run-full-ci` | Short form of `/tag-and-rerun-ci extra` (baseline + extra). Alias: `/rerun-full-ci` |
-| `/run-extra-ci` | Adds both labels + reruns **only** `PR Test Extra`, leaving baseline runs alone. Alias: `/rerun-extra-ci` |
+| `/run-<tier>-ci` | Adds `run-ci` and any configured tier label + reruns **only** the listed workflows (green ones included). E.g. `/run-extra-ci`. Alias: `/rerun-<tier>-ci` |
+| `/run-extra-ci <hardware>`, `/rerun-extra-ci <hardware>` | Equivalent to `/run-<hardware>-extra-ci` when that tier is registered; otherwise preserves the existing ignored-suffix behavior. |
 | `/rerun-test <test-file> [<test-file> ...]` | Reruns specific test file(s) via `rerun-test.yml`. A file arg containing a glob metacharacter (`*`, `?`, `[...]`) expands against `test/registered/` and the multimodal test dir to every matching `test_*.py` (e.g. `/rerun-test test_*backend*.py` — wrap in backticks so GitHub doesn't italicize the `*`); matches are deduped, grouped by dispatch shape, and can't carry a `::test` selector. No match → single ⛔ reply, nothing dispatched. |
 | `/rerun-group <group> [<group> ...]` | Expands registered test groups, then reuses `/rerun-test` |
 | `/run-cpu-ci` | Dispatches `run-cpu-ci.yml` on main: only the `base-a-test-cpu` suite, at the PR head SHA, no caches saved. Same gate as `/rerun-test`. Alias: `/rerun-cpu-ci` |
 
 Handled by `scripts/ci/utils/slash_command_handler.py` → `.github/workflows/slash-command-handler.yml`.
 
-### Label-gated workflow dispatch (pr-test, pr-test-extra)
+### Opt-in CI tiers (pr-test-extra and friends)
 
-`pr-test.yml` and `pr-test-extra.yml` both listen for `pull_request.labeled` (in addition to `opened`/`synchronize`/`reopened`). The `check-changes.if` gate has two clauses:
+The registry contains `extra`, including both `pr-test-extra.yml` (NVIDIA) and
+`pr-test-amd-extra.yml` (AMD), and `nv`, selecting NVIDIA base/shared checks.
+The shared extra label remains `run-ci-extra`; splitting hardware extra tiers
+is deferred. Other hardware selections such as `amd` and `ppu` are not registered.
+`/run-extra-ci amd` still runs the shared extra tier because `amd-extra` is absent.
 
-1. **For `labeled` events**: the just-added label must be one of the gating labels (`run-ci` for pr-test, `run-ci` or `run-ci-extra` for pr-test-extra) — otherwise every unrelated label addition would dispatch a full CI run.
-2. **All events**: the PR must currently carry the required labels.
+A selection with `label: null`, such as `nv`, adds only `run-ci` and leaves existing
+workflow gates intact. It selects existing runs for the current commit, skipping workflows with no run.
+Future pushes follow the existing workflow gates.
+These selections retain existing event/path conditions, including any limitations
+of rerunning old labeled events. Use `/run-ci nv` to select NVIDIA; legacy
+`/tag-and-rerun-ci nv` still retries broadly and adds no extra opt-in label.
 
-This is what lets `/tag-run-ci-label` (and the `extra` variant) trigger a fresh CI run without an extra push.
+An opt-in tier is a set of workflows a PR enters by carrying `run-ci-<tier>` on top of `run-ci`. Each tier is one entry in `scripts/ci/opt_in_ci_tiers.json`; the slash handler reads it for `/tag-run-ci-label <tier>`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci <tier>` and `/run-<tier>-ci`, so adding a tier needs no handler change. A tier's workflows follow one convention, enforced by `scripts/lint/check_opt_in_ci_tiers.py` (pre-commit):
 
-**Caveat — skipped runs cannot be un-skipped by `run.rerun()`:** GitHub's rerun API reuses the original event payload, so rerunning a `pull_request`-event run that was skipped because of missing labels will skip again (label set in the frozen payload doesn't update). The only way to recover a label-skipped run is to add the missing label, which fires a fresh `labeled` event with the current label set. `handle_rerun_failed_ci` in the slash handler is for rerunning failed/non-label-skipped runs; it cannot revive label-skipped ones.
+1. **Gate through `pr-gate.yml` with `require-label: run-ci-<tier>`.** The gate live-fetches labels, so a missing label fails the gate job (red run) and a rerun after labeling passes.
+2. **No `labeled` trigger.** GitHub's rerun API reuses the original event payload, so a run started by an unrelated label event and skipped by an `if` on that payload stays skipped on rerun. Adding a label after a push takes a rerun instead (`/tag-and-rerun-ci <tier>` or `/run-<tier>-ci`).
+3. **Every workflow that gates on the label is listed in the tier**, so `/run-<tier>-ci` re-runs all of them.
+
+Tier names `base`, `cpu`, `failed` and `full` are reserved: they collide with the
+base aliases, `/run-cpu-ci`, `/rerun-failed-ci` and `/run-full-ci`.
+Legacy labeling commands keep ignoring unknown suffixes; new `/run-ci <tier>`
+aliases reject unknown or multiple arguments before adding labels or rerunning.

 | Key | Grants |
 | --- | --- |
-| `can_tag_run_ci_label` | `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/run-full-ci`, `/run-extra-ci` |
-| `can_rerun_failed_ci` | `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/run-full-ci`, `/run-extra-ci` |
+| `can_tag_run_ci_label` | `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/run-full-ci`, `/run-<tier>-ci` |
+| `can_rerun_failed_ci` | `/rerun-failed-ci`, `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/run-full-ci`, `/run-<tier>-ci` |
 | `cooldown_interval_minutes` | rate limit in `pr-gate.yml`; `0` also grants `/rerun-test`, `/rerun-group`, `/run-cpu-ci` |
 
+`/run-ci`, `/run-base-ci`, and `/rerun-base-ci` with no argument are aliases of
+`/tag-and-rerun-ci`: labeling and retrying each use their existing permission
+checks. With one registered tier argument, they are aliases of `/run-<tier>-ci`
+and require both permissions. For example, `/run-ci extra` equals `/run-extra-ci`.
+Use `/run-ci nv` (or `/run-nv-ci`) for NVIDIA base and shared checks only.
+The `nv` entry has `label: null`, so it adds only `run-ci` and changes only the
+immediate rerun selection. Existing hardware labels are kept; future pushes follow the existing workflow gates.
+Legacy `/tag-and-rerun-ci <tier>` still retries broadly; its arguments add labels.
+
+`/run-extra-ci <hardware>` (also `/rerun-extra-ci <hardware>`) selects the
+`<hardware>-extra` tier only when it is registered. Otherwise, the existing
+ignored-suffix behavior is preserved. The registry contains `extra`, covering
+both NVIDIA and AMD extra workflows, and `nv`, selecting NVIDIA base/shared checks.
+The shared `extra` tier keeps `run-ci-extra`; separate hardware extra tiers are
+left for a follow-up. Other hardware-specific selections are not yet registered.
+
 `/rerun-test`, `/rerun-group` and `/run-cpu-ci` are gated on the commenter alone: either
 `cooldown_interval_minutes: 0`, or `write`/`admin` permission on the repo. Where
 the PR comes from makes no difference, and authoring it grants nothing.

+      # Live-fetch opt-in tier gate. Workflow-level `if` checks would read the

           REQUIRED_LABEL: ${{ inputs.require-label }}

+      require-label: run-ci-extra

        contains(github.event.comment.body, '/rerun-failed-ci') ||
        contains(github.event.comment.body, '/tag-and-rerun-ci') ||
+       contains(github.event.comment.body, '/run-ci') ||

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Check that scripts/ci/opt_in_ci_tiers.json matches the workflows it names.
+
+The slash command handler labels a PR and re-runs exactly the workflows listed
+for a tier. A workflow that gates on a tier label but is missing from the list
+is never re-run by /run-<tier>-ci; a listed workflow that gates on another
+label, or re-fires on `labeled`, cannot be recovered by a rerun.
+A null label is a selection of existing workflows with no extra opt-in gate;
+those workflows retain their existing event and path conditions.
+"""

+import glob
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+
+import yaml
+
+TIERS_FILE = "scripts/ci/opt_in_ci_tiers.json"
+PR_GATE = "./.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml"
+# Tier names become `/run-<tier>-ci`; these spellings are taken by other commands.
+RESERVED_TIER_NAMES = {"base", "cpu", "failed", "full"}
+_TIER_NAME = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$")
+
+
+def gate_labels(workflow: dict) -> set[str]:
+    """Labels a workflow requires through its pr-gate.yml calls."""
+    labels = set()
+    for job in (workflow.get("jobs") or {}).values():
+        if job.get("uses") == PR_GATE:
+            label = (job.get("with") or {}).get("require-label")
+            if label:
+                labels.add(label)
+    return labels
+
+
+def refires_on_labeled(workflow: dict) -> bool:
+    # yaml 1.1 parses the `on:` key as boolean True
+    triggers = workflow.get("on", workflow.get(True)) or {}
+    if not isinstance(triggers, dict):
+        return False
+    for event in ("pull_request", "pull_request_target"):
+        if "labeled" in ((triggers.get(event) or {}).get("types") or []):
+            return True
+    return False
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    with open(TIERS_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        tiers = json.load(f)
+
+    workflows = {}
+    for path in sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml")):
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
+            workflows[path] = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
+
+    errors = []
+    for name, tier in tiers.items():
+        label = tier["label"]
+        listed = tier["workflows"]
+        if not _TIER_NAME.match(name) or name in RESERVED_TIER_NAMES:
+            errors.append(f"tier `{name}`: invalid or reserved tier name")
+        if label is not None and label != f"run-ci-{name}":
+            errors.append(
+                f"tier `{name}`: label must be `run-ci-{name}`, got `{label}`"
+            )
+        if not listed:
+            errors.append(f"tier `{name}`: lists no workflows")
+
+        for path in listed:
+            if path not in workflows:
+                errors.append(f"tier `{name}`: {path} does not exist")
+                continue
+            if label is None:
+                if gate_labels(workflows[path]):
+                    errors.append(
+                        f"tier `{name}`: {path} requires an opt-in label, "
+                        "but the selection has label: null"
+                    )
+                continue
+            if label not in gate_labels(workflows[path]):
+                errors.append(
+                    f"tier `{name}`: {path} does not call pr-gate.yml "
+                    f"with `require-label: {label}`"
+                )
+            if refires_on_labeled(workflows[path]):
+                errors.append(
+                    f"tier `{name}`: {path} triggers on `labeled`; a rerun of "
+                    "a run started by an unrelated label stays skipped"
+                )
+
+        for path, workflow in workflows.items():
+            if label in gate_labels(workflow) and path not in listed:
+                errors.append(
+                    f"tier `{name}`: {path} gates on `{label}` but is not "
+                    f"listed, so /run-{name}-ci never re-runs it"
+                )
+
+    if errors:
+        print(f"ERROR: {TIERS_FILE} is out of sync with .github/workflows:")
+        for error in errors:
+            print(f"  {error}")
+        return 1
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
